steps.intent: Panama’s objective is to renew and sharpen the targeted Haiti sanctions regime while keeping the Council focused on humanitarian access, protection of children and support for the GSF; the draft reflects Panama’s co-penholder role with the United States and its emphasis on regional solidarity. The difficult points will be the expanded designation criteria, especially obstruction of humanitarian access and sexual and gender-based violence, and the arms-embargo language, where Russia and China may seek softer formulations and some members will insist on clear humanitarian carve-outs. The draft is calibrated to retain at least nine positive votes and avoid a veto by reaffirming Haitian sovereignty, consent and international-law safeguards.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the targeted measures and the extension of the Panel of Experts, and welcomes the text's focus on humanitarian access and arms diversion. We request that OP7 include clear and credible evidence and fair and clear listing and delisting procedures, and that OP11 strengthen safeguards against diversion of authorized arms transfers. We also ask for OP10 to ensure humanitarian exemption requests are processed without undue delay and for reporting on unintended humanitarian impact.
messages.China: China supports renewal of the targeted 2653 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which remain important to curbing gang violence and arms trafficking. However, China abstained on resolution 2793 and cannot join language welcoming or endorsing the GSF without clear safeguards. We request that references to the GSF be changed to take note and be expressly limited to resolution 2793, with the consent and close coordination of the Government of Haiti, strict compliance with international law and HRDDP, and reporting on compliance and funding. We also ask for a clearer, prompt humanitarian exemption process.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and welcomes the draft’s strong humanitarian, child-protection and accountability language. We ask the penholders to strengthen OP5 and OP14 with explicit reporting on international law compliance and HRDDP, and to add the 2793 language treating children associated with gangs as victims and ensuring referral and reintegration. We also suggest tightening OP11’s notification requirement to prevent arms diversion.
messages.France: France thanks Panama and the United States for this balanced text and supports renewal of the sanctions regime. We ask for two targeted additions: include narcotics trafficking and money laundering among the designation criteria, and ensure the Secretary-General reports on GSF compliance with international law and child protection, so that the strengthened mandate is matched by clear accountability.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and welcomes the strengthened designation criteria, especially on humanitarian obstruction, sexual and gender-based violence and recruitment of children. We would like the text to reinforce humanitarian safeguards, require advance notification and end-use monitoring for arms-embargo exceptions, and strengthen reporting on arms diversion and humanitarian impact. These changes would improve the resolution’s consistency with the human rights and protection priorities Greece advanced during the negotiation of resolution 2793 (2025).
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the Haiti sanctions regime and appreciates the penholders’ inclusive approach. We request that OP7 retain the natural-resources designation hook agreed in resolution 2752 (2024), and that OP5 explicitly reference the 2024 Handover Protocol, consistent with the A3+ priority on child protection. With these adjustments, we can support the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports renewing the targeted sanctions and humanitarian safeguards in this draft. We ask the penholders to strengthen reporting and oversight of the GSF, including human rights and child-protection compliance and sustainable financing, while reaffirming Haitian ownership. With these improvements Pakistan can support the text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the balanced renewal of the sanctions regime and the draft’s focus on the GSF, humanitarian access and Haitian ownership. We would ask for two refinements: prior notification for OP11 exemptions to help prevent arms diversion, and OP14 reporting on GSF operationalization and compliance with international law, including the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. With these adjustments, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports renewing the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts. However, we abstained on resolution 2793 and cannot accept language in this technical renewal that welcomes or endorses the GSF; 'taking note' is the correct formulation. We also insist that designations be evidence-based and that reporting cover GSF funding and readiness. With these adjustments, we can join consensus.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts, and we thank Panama and the United States for the balanced text. We ask the penholder to strengthen the draft's political transition and BINUH language, make GSF support predictable, and reinforce child protection and humanitarian safeguards. These changes would align the text with the A3+ position and the Council's commitments in resolution 2793 (2025).
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports renewing the targeted sanctions and welcomes the draft's focus on humanitarian access and human rights. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 with explicit child-protection and referral safeguards, and OP14 with reporting on human rights and child-protection compliance. We would also prefer OP4 to reflect unified UN coordination through the Special Representative of the Secretary-General.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as circulated. We welcome the renewal of targeted sanctions with clear humanitarian carve-outs and the call for swift operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force in coordination with Haitian authorities, BINUH and the UN country team. We stress that sanctions must remain targeted and must not impede humanitarian access or the delivery of basic services.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and thanks Panama and the United States for bringing this text forward. We would like two modest but important strengthenings: explicit recognition that sexual and gender-based violence is used as a tool of control and coercion, and reporting by the Secretary-General on human rights compliance, child protection and protection of civilians. These changes would reinforce the rights-compliant approach the Council has already set out for the Gang Suppression Force and help ensure sanctions do not impede humanitarian access.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports this draft as a strong basis and appreciates Panama’s co-penholdership. We would like targeted adjustments to reflect the terrorist nature of the most dangerous gangs, to make the arms embargo explicit on small arms and light weapons, and to ensure reporting covers GSF operationalization and sanctions implementation. We ask the penholder to incorporate these changes and can support the text once they are reflected.

replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: OP12 requires advance notification; OP15 covers GSF operationalization and international law and HRDDP compliance.
replies.Russian Federation: accepted: PP5 and OP5 use take-note language and strict mandate and sovereignty language; OP8 requires substantiated evidence; OP15 covers funding, readiness and results.

steps.summary: The revised text retains Panama's core priorities of renewed targeted sanctions, humanitarian safeguards and support for the GSF while accommodating permanent-member concerns through take-note and strict-compliance language. Consolidated reporting, child-protection, arms-diversion and political-process provisions address the broad requests and allow consensus.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating its key concerns on evidence-based designations, fair delisting, expedited humanitarian exemptions and safeguards against arms diversion. The text strikes an appropriate balance between supporting Haitian-led security efforts and preserving Haiti's sovereignty, while strengthening humanitarian access and protection of civilians. Algeria therefore supports the draft as it stands and will vote in favour.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for accommodating its concerns on resolution 2793, the limits of the GSF mandate, Haitian consent and coordination, and reporting on compliance and funding. The current text is balanced and properly focuses on sanctions renewal, humanitarian access, child protection and a Haitian-led political process. China supports the current draft and will vote in favour. We encourage full implementation and continued reporting to the Council.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current text and is ready to vote in favour. We appreciate that the penholders incorporated our key concerns on HRDDP compliance, child protection and reporting in OP6 and OP15, and we welcome the strengthened humanitarian carve-out and prior notification safeguards. Full implementation, monitoring and accountability will be essential, as will unhindered humanitarian access and protection of civilians. Denmark encourages all members to support adoption.
messages.France: France welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of its previous concerns in OP8 and OP15, particularly on narcotics, money laundering, GSF compliance with international law and child protection reporting. The draft preserves the GSF’s mandate without expansion, maintains essential humanitarian safeguards and strengthens the sanctions regime in support of Haiti’s stability. France supports the text as it stands and calls for its adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft. We thank the penholders for incorporating our earlier requests on expedited humanitarian exemptions, prior notification and end-use safeguards, and arms-diversion reporting. We welcome the strong provisions on human rights, child protection, humanitarian access, and GSF compliance and reporting, and we call for swift operationalization of the GSF under the coordination of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Greece will vote in favour.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks Panama and the United States for the revised text and for incorporating our earlier requests on the natural-resources designation criteria and the 2024 Handover Protocol. We support the draft as it stands, as it contains the safeguards we sought on human rights, child protection, humanitarian access, and GSF compliance and reporting. We will vote in favour.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for incorporating our key concerns on predictable and sustainable support, compliance and oversight, child protection, and comprehensive reporting in OP5, OP6 and OP15. The current text remains focused on renewing the targeted sanctions regime, preserving humanitarian carve-outs, strengthening arms-embargo implementation, and reaffirming that the GSF operates without an expanded mandate and in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty. Pakistan therefore supports the draft as it stands and will vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the co-penholders for the revised draft and for reflecting our earlier concerns through the advance notification requirement in OP12 and the reporting on GSF operationalization and international law, including human rights and HRDDP compliance, in OP15. We support the current text as balanced and operational, and we encourage the Council to proceed toward swift adoption. Korea remains ready to support implementation and continued Council engagement on Haiti.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation takes note that our key concerns have been reflected in revision 1: the Council takes note of resolution 2793 (2025), the GSF is kept within its authorized mandate and Haitian sovereignty, designations require clear and substantiated evidence, and reporting covers funding and operational results. We can support the current text. We will expect strict implementation of the humanitarian carve-outs and full respect for Haitian sovereignty and the Council’s non-expansion of the GSF mandate.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft as it stands and welcomes the incorporation of our priorities, including the Haitian-led political process, predictable support for the GSF, strengthened child protection, and streamlined humanitarian procedures. We thank the penholder for the constructive engagement and encourage the Council to proceed to adoption without further delay.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text. We welcome the incorporation of our priorities on child protection and referral, prevention of detention of children with adults, support for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, HRDDP compliance and reporting, and overall coordination by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. We encourage the Council to remain united behind full implementation of resolution 2793 (2025) and the renewed sanctions measures.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as circulated. We welcome the targeted sanctions, strong humanitarian carve-outs, and continued reporting on the GSF and human rights compliance. We encourage partners to provide predictable support to the GSF and remain firm on Haiti's sovereignty and regional coordination.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current draft and thanks Panama and the United States for their leadership. We welcome the strong language on sexual and gender-based violence as a tool of control and coercion, child protection, humanitarian access and human rights compliance reporting. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and urge partners to provide predictable support for the GSF and for implementation of the sanctions measures.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of our priorities on terrorist activities, small arms and light weapons, expedited designations, and reporting on GSF operationalization and sanctions implementation. The text maintains the necessary balance between robust sanctions enforcement and humanitarian carve-outs while preserving the GSF mandate in resolution 2793 (2025). We call for consensus adoption.

steps.summary: All Council members that submitted comments support the draft as revised and requested no further changes. Revision 2 therefore retains the text unchanged from revision 1. The draft is expected to be adopted unanimously.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently voted in favour of Haiti resolutions, supported the current draft in negotiations with no requested changes, and would back a targeted sanctions renewal that upholds Haitian sovereignty and humanitarian safeguards. A pre-vote explanation is consistent with Algeria’s emphasis on sovereignty, non-expansion of mandates, and humanitarian access.
reasons.China: China’s last-round position was support with no requested changes, and the draft contains safeguards on sovereignty, sanctions, humanitarian access and GSF compliance that align with China’s stated concerns after abstaining on resolution 2793.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported resolution 2793 and this text aligns with its priorities on strict compliance with international law, child protection, humanitarian access, targeted sanctions, and a Haitian-led political process.
reasons.France: France supports renewing targeted sanctions and operationalizing the GSF while stressing humanitarian access, human rights compliance, and a Haitian-led political process. Voting in favour aligns with France’s consistent record on Haiti and its support for the Panama/US penholders.
reasons.Greece: Greece supported resolution 2793 and the current draft aligns with its emphasis on human rights, humanitarian access, and a coordinated international response to Haiti’s security crisis. It requested no changes and signaled support in negotiations, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported the Haiti sanctions regime and the recent GSF transition, and the draft incorporates key humanitarian, child-protection, and due-diligence safeguards that align with Guyana's stated priorities. No pre-vote explanation is needed given Guyana's clear support and the consensus-oriented negotiations.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan indicated support in the final negotiation round and made no additional requests. The draft renews targeted sanctions with humanitarian safeguards and does not expand the GSF mandate, aligning with Pakistan’s concerns and its commitment to Haiti’s stability.
reasons.Panama: Panama is the co-penholder of the draft and has consistently supported the Haiti sanctions and security resolutions, so it votes yes and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported Security Council action on Haiti, including the sanctions regime and the transition to the Gang Suppression Force, and the draft is consistent with its prior votes and statements. As all members indicated support and no concerns were raised, it would vote in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft is primarily a targeted sanctions renewal with strengthened humanitarian safeguards and reports, consistent with Russia's prior support for Haiti sanctions resolutions; Russia can back it while reiterating caveats on the GSF and arms trafficking.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported Security Council action on Haiti and the draft aligns with its priorities on sanctions, humanitarian access, and accountability; no specific concerns required a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported Council action on Haiti, including the GSF transition and targeted sanctions, and the draft includes strong human rights, child protection and humanitarian safeguards. With no outstanding requests, Slovenia supports the text and votes in favour without a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia had already indicated support with no requested changes, consistent with its priorities on targeted sanctions, sovereignty, humanitarian access and accountable security support. As an elected member with experience in peace operations, it would vote yes and explain its support.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom has consistently supported Council action on Haiti, including the GSF and sanctions framework, and the draft aligns with UK priorities on human rights, humanitarian access, child protection, and accountability. There is no reason for the UK to abstain or veto.
reasons.United States of America: The United States co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported renewing Haiti sanctions and backing the Gang Suppression Force. All positions indicated support, and the text aligns with U.S. policy and prior statements.

before.Algeria: Algeria votes in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our firm commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of Haiti, and to the principle that the Government and people of Haiti must remain in the lead in addressing the crisis. Algeria supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo, which must be implemented without hampering humanitarian assistance or basic services and with clear, expedited humanitarian exemptions. We underscore the need for unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, especially children and women, and full accountability. The Gang Suppression Force must operate strictly within resolution 2793 (2025), with the consent and close coordination of the Haitian authorities, under international human rights law and with robust oversight, and its mandate must not be expanded. We also stress that security measures cannot substitute for an inclusive, Haitian-led political process aimed at restoring democratic institutions and preparing free and fair elections. Algeria will continue to support Haiti’s sovereignty, stability and humanitarian relief.
before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The situation in Haiti remains grave, and the international community must support the Haitian people while fully respecting Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity. China supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts as important tools to curb arms trafficking and gang violence. At the same time, sanctions must be implemented with clear safeguards and must not impede humanitarian assistance. We emphasize that the Gang Suppression Force must operate strictly within the mandate authorized by the Council, in full compliance with international law, including international human rights law and humanitarian law, and with the consent and close coordination of the Government of Haiti. The international community should provide adequate and predictable support, and the political process must remain Haitian-led and Haitian-owned. China hopes that the resolution just introduced will help advance security, protect civilians, especially children and vulnerable groups, and create conditions for a political settlement and free and fair elections in Haiti.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, including the provisions intended to safeguard humanitarian assistance and expedite exemptions. Denmark supports the operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force in strict compliance with international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law and the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We underline the importance of child protection, the referral of children associated with gangs to reintegration programmes, protection of survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, and robust oversight and accountability. We urge all partners to provide predictable support and to advance an inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to free and fair elections.
before.France: La France votera en faveur du projet de résolution. Nous saluons le travail des co-pénholders et soutenons le renouvellement du régime de sanctions, en particulier les dispositions visant à prévenir le détournement d’armes et à préserver l’accès humanitaire. Nous appelons à la mise en œuvre intégrale de la résolution 2793 (2025), dans le strict respect du droit international, y compris des droits de l’homme, et à un processus politique inclusif, conduit par les Haïtiens, en vue d’élections libres et régulières.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the strengthened provisions on humanitarian access, protection of civilians, child protection, and accountability. Greece attaches particular importance to strict compliance by the Gang Suppression Force with international law, including international human rights law and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and to close coordination under the overall coordination of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. We also stress that sanctions must remain targeted and must not impede humanitarian assistance, and we call on all partners to provide predictable support for the Force’s swift and effective operationalization.
before.Panama: Panamá votará a favor del proyecto de resolución que hemos presentado junto con los Estados Unidos. La crisis en Haití exige una respuesta decidida del Consejo: la plena operacionalización de la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas, el acceso humanitario sin obstáculos, la protección de los civiles, en particular niños, niñas y mujeres, y sanciones selectivas eficaces contra quienes alimentan la violencia y el tráfico de armas. Reafirmamos nuestro respeto a la soberanía, independencia e integridad territorial de Haití y nuestro compromiso con una solución haitiana e inclusiva que conduzca a elecciones libres y justas. Instamos a todos los miembros a apoyar este texto para que el Consejo envíe un mensaje claro: Haití no está solo.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will support this draft resolution. We believe that renewing the targeted sanctions regime, including the arms embargo, is necessary to help stem the illicit flows of weapons and ammunition that continue to fuel gang violence and undermine stability in Haiti. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must remain targeted, must not harm the civilian population, and must not impede humanitarian assistance. We also emphasize that the Gang Suppression Force must act strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), without expanding that mandate, and in full compliance with international law and the protection of civilians. Ultimately, the situation in Haiti cannot be resolved by security measures alone; it requires an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, the restoration of democratic institutions, and preparations for free and fair elections. We call on all Member States, especially those in the region, to take concrete action against arms trafficking and diversion into Haiti.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia welcomes this draft resolution’s renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which are important tools to curb illicit arms trafficking and gang violence in Haiti. We support the operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force strictly in accordance with resolution 2793 (2025) and in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, with robust human rights, child protection and accountability safeguards. We stress the need for unhindered humanitarian access and an inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to free and fair elections. Somalia will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the deteriorating security and humanitarian situation in Haiti and condemn in the strongest terms the violence, sexual and gender-based violence, attacks on civilians, children, medical facilities and humanitarian personnel, and the recruitment and use of children by gangs. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo, alongside vital humanitarian carve-outs, and we stress the importance of full compliance by the Gang Suppression Force with international law, including international human rights law, and the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. The Council must continue to support Haiti’s sovereignty and stability, unhindered humanitarian access, accountability, child protection and a Haitian-led political process leading to free and fair elections.
before.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the draft resolution before the Council and will vote in favour. We thank Panama for its co-penmanship and all Council members for their constructive engagement. This text renews targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, strengthens measures against arms trafficking and those who obstruct humanitarian assistance, and supports the operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force without expanding its mandate. We urge Member States and partners to provide the GSF with the personnel, financing and logistics required to fulfil its mandate. At the same time, the United States underscores that all operations must be conducted in strict compliance with international law, including international human rights law and child protection obligations. The United States remains committed to Haiti’s sovereignty, stability and a Haitian-led political process leading to free and fair elections.

after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the A3+ — Algeria, Sierra Leone, Somalia and my own country, Guyana.

The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which renews the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts at a time when Haiti continues to face a grave security and humanitarian crisis. We thank Panama and the United States for their efforts as co-penholders and all Council members for their constructive engagement.

We support the renewal of the arms embargo and the targeted sanctions, which remain essential tools to curb illicit arms trafficking and the gang violence that continues to devastate Haitian communities. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must remain targeted and must not impede humanitarian assistance or basic services. In this regard, we welcome the humanitarian safeguards and exemptions reflected in the text.

The A3+ also underscores that the Gang Suppression Force must operate strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity, and with the consent and close coordination of the Haitian authorities, under the overall coordination of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Its operations must comply fully with international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and with the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Robust safeguards for children, including the treatment of children associated with gangs as victims and their referral to child protection and reintegration programmes, as well as protection and support for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, remain central.

We call for predictable and adequate voluntary contributions, personnel and logistical support for the Force so that it can fulfil its mandate effectively. We also emphasize that security measures alone cannot resolve the crisis. An inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, leading to free and fair elections and the restoration of democratic institutions, remains indispensable. Accountability, unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, especially children, women and girls, must remain at the heart of our collective response.

The A3+ reaffirms its solidarity with the people of Haiti. The Council’s unanimous message today must translate into tangible support for their aspirations for peace, dignity and stability.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. Our vote reflects our support for the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to curb the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition that continue to fuel gang violence and instability in Haiti. We also welcome the humanitarian safeguards in the text, and we stress that sanctions must remain targeted, must not harm the civilian population, and must not impede humanitarian assistance.

Pakistan reaffirms its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of Haiti. The primary responsibility for security and stability rests with the Government and people of Haiti, and international efforts must be conducted with the consent and close coordination of the Haitian authorities. We underscore that the Gang Suppression Force must operate strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), without any expansion, and in full compliance with international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law, as applicable, as well as the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. The protection of civilians, in particular children, women and girls, and the treatment of children associated with armed gangs as victims must remain central.

We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation, including the closure of humanitarian operations and attacks on medical personnel and facilities. We call for unhindered, safe and timely humanitarian access and for the protection of humanitarian actors. We also reiterate the need for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process leading to free and fair elections and the restoration of democratic institutions.

Pakistan will continue to support the people of Haiti and constructive Council action aimed at promoting peace, stability and dignity in the country.
after.Panama:
Señor Presidente,

Panamá agradece a los Estados Unidos, nuestro copatrocinador, y a todos los miembros del Consejo por su constructivo compromiso, que ha permitido la adopción unánime de esta resolución. Este resultado envía un mensaje claro: la comunidad internacional no permanece indiferente ante el sufrimiento del pueblo haitiano.

La renovación del régimen de sanciones selectivas y del mandato del Panel de Expertos, junto con medidas reforzadas contra el tráfico ilícito de armas y quienes obstruyen la asistencia humanitaria, es un instrumento esencial para frenar la violencia de las pandillas y proteger a los civiles. Reiteramos que estas sanciones están dirigidas contra quienes alimentan la violencia y no contra la población haitiana, y deben aplicarse con salvaguardias y exenciones humanitarias claras y expeditas.

Panamá insta a la plena y rápida operacionalización de la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas, estrictamente dentro del mandato de la resolución 2793 (2025), con el consentimiento y la estrecha coordinación del Gobierno de Haití, la Policía Nacional Haitiana, las fuerzas armadas haitianas, la BINUH y el Representante Especial del Secretario General. Su actuación debe cumplir plenamente el derecho internacional, incluidos los derechos humanos y el derecho internacional humanitario, así como la política de diligencia debida de las Naciones Unidas, con especial atención a la protección de la niñez, la referenciación de niños asociados a pandillas a programas de reintegración, la atención a sobrevivientes de violencia sexual y de género y la rendición de cuentas.

Reafirmamos nuestro respeto a la soberanía, independencia, integridad territorial y unidad de Haití. Apoyamos un proceso político inclusivo, liderado y apropiado por los haitianos, que conduzca a elecciones libres y justas y al restablecimiento de las instituciones democráticas. Asimismo, subrayamos la urgencia de garantizar un acceso humanitario sin obstáculos, seguro y oportuno, y de proteger al personal humanitario y a las instalaciones médicas.

Panamá seguirá trabajando para mantener la atención del Consejo sobre Haití y para que esta resolución se traduzca en acciones concretas sobre el terreno. Haití no está solo.
after.Republic of Korea:
The Republic of Korea voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its unanimous adoption. We thank Panama and the United States for their co-penmanship and all Council members for their constructive engagement.

We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to curb the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms, ammunition and related materiel that fuel gang violence in Haiti. At the same time, sanctions must remain targeted, with clear and expedited humanitarian exemptions, and must not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance or basic services to the Haitian people.

The Republic of Korea also stresses that the Gang Suppression Force must be operationalized strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), without expanding that mandate, and in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and unity. Its operations must comply fully with international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law, as applicable, and with the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We attach particular importance to child protection, the treatment of children associated with armed gangs as victims, their referral to child protection actors and reintegration programmes, and the protection and support of survivors of sexual and gender-based violence.

We urge Member States and partners to provide adequate, predictable and sustainable voluntary contributions, personnel and logistics so that the Force can fulfil its mandate effectively. Without security, humanitarian access and a credible political process cannot be sustained. We therefore call for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process aimed at restoring democratic institutions and preparing free and fair elections.

The Republic of Korea will continue to support the people of Haiti and to work with the Council and regional partners towards a stable, peaceful and prosperous Haiti.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the A3+, namely Algeria, Guyana, Somalia and my own country, Sierra Leone. The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We voted in favour because we believe these measures are important tools to curb the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition that continue to fuel gang violence and undermine the stability of Haiti. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must remain targeted and must not harm the civilian population or impede humanitarian assistance, and that clear and expedited humanitarian exemptions must be ensured.

The A3+ strongly condemns the continuing gang violence, including attacks against civilians, children, women and girls, medical facilities and humanitarian personnel. We are deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation, including the closure of humanitarian operations in Port-au-Prince, and we call for unhindered, safe and timely humanitarian access to all populations in need. We reaffirm our strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of Haiti, and to the principle that the Government and people of Haiti must remain in the lead in addressing the crisis.

We take note of the authorization of the Gang Suppression Force in resolution 2793 (2025). The GSF must operate strictly within that mandate, without expansion, and in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, with the consent and close coordination of the Government of Haiti, the Haitian National Police, the Haitian armed forces, BINUH and the United Nations country team, under the overall coordination of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Its operations must comply strictly with international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law, as applicable, and with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We underline the importance of child protection, the implementation of the 2024 Handover Protocol, the referral of children associated with gangs to child protection and reintegration programmes, and the referral of survivors of sexual and gender-based violence to protection and support services. We also call on Member States and partners to provide adequate, predictable and sustainable voluntary contributions, personnel and logistics to the GSF.

Finally, the A3+ emphasizes that security measures alone cannot resolve the crisis in Haiti. We call for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, with the good offices of BINUH and in coordination with regional partners, aimed at preparing free and fair elections and restoring democratic institutions. The A3+ will continue to stand with the people of Haiti in their pursuit of peace, stability and a better future.
after.Slovenia:
Slovenia voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome its adoption and the Council’s continued unity in support of the people of Haiti. The security and humanitarian situation remains deeply alarming, and we condemn in the strongest terms the continued gang violence, attacks on civilians, humanitarian personnel and medical facilities, sexual and gender-based violence, and the recruitment and use of children. The closure of Doctors Without Borders operations in Port-au-Prince is a further warning of the intolerable conditions faced by humanitarians.

We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo, which must remain targeted, include effective humanitarian safeguards, and not harm the civilian population. The Gang Suppression Force must operate strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), without expansion, in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and in close coordination with the Government of Haiti and under the overall coordination of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General. Its operations must comply fully with international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Child protection, the 2024 Handover Protocol, referral of children to reintegration programmes, protection and support for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, and robust oversight and accountability must remain central.

We underline the need for unhindered, safe and timely humanitarian access and for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process leading to free and fair elections. We urge all partners to provide predictable financial, personnel and logistical support to the Force and to address the gaps identified by the Secretary-General. Slovenia remains committed to supporting Haiti’s sovereignty, stability and the protection of all civilians.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. We are pleased that the Council has renewed the targeted sanctions regime and arms embargo while preserving essential humanitarian carve-outs, and we thank Panama and the United States for their leadership. We now look to the full and effective implementation of resolution 2793 (2025), including the swift operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force in strict compliance with international law, international human rights law and the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. The United Kingdom will continue to support Haiti’s sovereignty and stability, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians—especially children and survivors of sexual and gender-based violence—and an inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to free and fair elections.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution, which we were proud to co-penhold with Panama. Today the Council has spoken with one voice in support of the Haitian people and in opposition to the gangs, traffickers, and armed actors who continue to terrorize civilians and undermine Haiti’s stability.

This text renews the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, strengthens measures against illicit arms trafficking, preserves essential humanitarian carve-outs, and supports the full operationalization of the Gang Suppression Force strictly within the mandate set out in resolution 2793 (2025), without expanding that mandate. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and again commend Kenya’s leadership, the troop- and police-contributing countries, the Caribbean Community, the Organization of American States, and all partners supporting Haiti.

The United States stresses that the GSF must act in strict compliance with international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and the United Nations Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Child protection must remain central, including implementation of the 2024 Handover Protocol, referral of children associated with armed gangs to protection and reintegration actors, and ensuring that survivors of sexual and gender-based violence receive protection and support.

The Council’s adoption of this resolution must now be matched by action. We urge Member States and partners to provide the GSF with the personnel, financing, logistics, and capabilities it needs, and we encourage the Standing Group of Partners to help coordinate that support. We also call on Haitian stakeholders, with the good offices of BINUH and in coordination with regional partners, to advance an inclusive, Haitian-led political process aimed at free and fair elections and the restoration of democratic institutions.

The United States remains committed to Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and unity, and to working with the Haitian Government and international partners to protect civilians, improve security, and create the conditions for a stable and democratic Haiti.
